ThingDef.label: AKN GP-25 (PU-1)
ThingDef.description:
Caliber: 7.62x39mm. 30-round detachable mag. Select-Fire.
The AK (Avtomat Kalashnikova) is a Soviet assault rifle designed between 1946-1947 by Mikhail Kalashnikov. Commonly (and somewhat anachronistically) known as the "AK-47," the AK is one of the most recognizable and widely used weapons platforms ever made, with over 100 million Kalashnikov-type guns having been produced since 1948. Reputed for its ease of mass production and reliability, the AK was the backbone of the Soviet Armed Forces and continues to be the standard service platform in most former Warsaw Pact nations.
The early line of AK rifles consists of three major variants - the Type I (produced from 1948/49 to 1951), Type II (1951-1954/55), and Type III (1955-1959.) Type I AKs had stamped sheet metal receivers, while the subsequent Type II had a milled receiver. The Type III was a further update that lightened the milled receiver. This rifle is a Type III, which was the most widely produced of the early models. Most of the widely produced international variants of the early AK (such as the East German MPi-K, Chinese Type 56, and North Korean Type 58) were based on the Type III configuration.
The AKN variant has a Warsaw Pact rail on the left side of the receiver, allowing it to mount various optics. Fitted with a GP-25 40mm grenade launcher and a PU-1 telescopic scope.

li.label: GP-25
li.description: Caliber: 40mm VOG-25. 1-round tube. Single shot. The GP-25 is a Russian 40mm grenade launcher designed in the 1960s, as part of several independent worldwide efforts to replace the need for rifle grenades. It can be fitted onto almost every major AK variant that exists, as well as a few non-AK rifles (such as the AN-94.) Other derivatives of the GP-25 include the later GP-30 and GP-34.
